findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test (or documented rationale for why it is deferred/untestable) that exercises the loser-fallback path — e.g. pre-seed the lock directory to force a worker down the poll/fallback branch and assert it still renders correctly within the deadline.
evidence: Approach: 'Losers poll; a loser that observes neither the lock nor an artifact re-enters the os.mkdir acquisition loop' and 'a crashed winner degrades to today's per-worker behaviour rather than deadlocking'
Testing lists happy path, serial path, digest/edge mutation, and whole-suite regression — but no scenario that leaves a stale lock dir or forces the loser-fallback branch
findings.finding: The plan introduces a new cross-worker mutex (os.mkdir lock, loser polling, 150s fallback, crashed-winner degradation) but the Testing section exercises only the digest/cache-hit correctness paths (corpus mutation, protected-fragment break, happy/serial runs). The loser-fallback and crashed-winner-lock-left-behind paths — the riskiest new logic — get no described test, so a bug in the lock acquisition or fallback deadline could ship undetected.
findings.location: Testing section / Approach 'Mutual exclusion uses os.mkdir ... The loser's fallback deadline is 150s'
scenarios: A regression in the loser-fallback deadline or lock-cleanup finally block passes the described tests (which only ever have a fast winner) yet deadlocks or re-renders unnecessarily under a real crashed-winner condition in CI.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how a stale lock directory left by a SIGKILLed/timed-out winner is reclaimed within the session (e.g. a lock-age/mtime staleness check that lets a loser steal a lock older than the winner-fill bound) so losers do not each burn the full 150s deadline on a dead winner.
evidence: 'removes the lock directory in a `finally` block so it is retired on both the success and the error path' — a finally does not execute on SIGKILL/OS-timeout kill

'a loser blocked on a crashed or pathologically slow winner renders locally and still finishes inside the timeout' — describes local fallback but not retirement of the orphaned lock dir within the session
findings.finding: The lock-directory retirement relies on a `finally` block, which does not run when the winner is SIGKILLed or killed by the --timeout=300 guard; the resulting orphan lock directory forces every subsequent loser in the session to poll the full 150s deadline before rendering locally, and no consumer is described as reclaiming or timing-out the stale lock itself.
findings.location: Approach — 'removes the lock directory in a `finally` block' / 'a loser that observes neither the lock nor an artifact re-enters the os.mkdir acquisition loop'
scenarios: A worker holding the lock is killed by the 300s guard or OOM; every other consumer then waits 150s on the dead lock before its own local render, and the orphan lock dir is never cleaned until pytest rotates the session temp dir
findings.suggested_fix: Add a staleness check to the acquisition/poll loop: if the lock directory's mtime exceeds a bound (e.g. > winner-fill-time), treat it as abandoned, remove it, and re-attempt os.mkdir — and state this in the Approach and an AC.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Anchor the timing ACs (2/3/4) to a baseline re-measured on the CI runner, or reframe them as structural checks (exactly one _rendered() consumer shows a fill; the other three drop by an order of magnitude relative to the same run's own baseline) rather than absolute macOS-worktree seconds.
evidence: 'Aggregate test-call time for the module under that command is at least 40% below the 212s baseline recorded above' — 212s is a macOS-worktree figure
'No single test in the module exceeds 120s under -n 3' — absolute wall-clock threshold read from --durations on CI hardware
'Measured on this worktree (macOS, pandoc 3.6.1 ...)' — baselines are local, not CI-hardware
findings.finding: Acceptance criteria 2, 3, and 4 assert timing thresholds (exactly one >10s duration, >=40% below a 212s baseline, no test >120s) that were measured on 'this worktree (macOS, pandoc 3.6.1)'; they are read off --durations on CI hardware whose absolute pandoc-spawn timings may differ, and no CI-hardware baseline or tolerance is stated, so these ACs may be non-deterministic on the actual runner.
scenarios: CI runner is slower/faster than the macOS worktree, so a single fill legitimately exceeds 120s or the aggregate does not clear the 40% bar despite the caching working correctly
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe AC2/AC4 relative to the same CI run's own before/after (e.g. 'three fills before -> one fill after in the same runner's --durations'), and record the absolute 40% figure as evidence rather than a hard pass/fail gate.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify the hand-rolled os.mkdir lock against the established pytest-xdist session-fixture recipe (getbasetemp().parent + filelock.FileLock, already installed): either adopt filelock or state concretely why the bespoke mkdir + 150s-deadline crash-degradation behaviour is preferable.
evidence: pytest-xdist official how-to.rst: 'get the temp directory shared by all workers root_tmp_dir = tmp_path_factory.getbasetemp().parent ... with FileLock(str(fn) + ".lock")' (github.com/pytest-dev/pytest-xdist/blob/master/docs/how-to.rst, retrieved this run)
resolve_symbol: 'EXISTS: filelock resolves in the installed environment [site-packages]' — the dependency the canonical recipe uses is already available, so no new dependency is required to adopt it
The plan text never names pytest-xdist's session-fixture recipe or filelock, and gives no Rule-of-Three / anti-repackaging justification for a bespoke lock over the established one

The plan's sharing idiom ('.parent is pytest-<N> ... shared by every worker of THIS session') is verbatim the documented pattern, confirming the plan is in the same design space as the prior art it omits
findings.finding: The plan reinvents cross-worker mutual exclusion with a hand-rolled os.mkdir lock-directory, polling loop, and 150s fallback deadline, without considering the established prior art: pytest-xdist's own documented 'Making session-scoped fixtures execute only once' recipe uses tmp_path_factory.getbasetemp().parent (which the plan already adopts) together with filelock.FileLock for the lock, and filelock is already installed in this environment.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Mutual exclusion uses os.mkdir on a sibling lock directory ... Losers poll ... The loser's fallback deadline is 150s'
scenarios: Author implements a bespoke mkdir/poll/deadline lock that must handle crash-recovery, TOCTOU, and stale-lock cleanup by hand — logic filelock.FileLock already provides and battle-tests
Reviewers cannot tell whether the hand-rolled 150s-deadline crash-degradation behaviour is a deliberate improvement over filelock or an unaware reinvention
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach, cite pytest-xdist's 'Making session-scoped fixtures execute only once' how-to and note that filelock is already available; then either replace the os.mkdir lock with filelock.FileLock (keeping the digest-keyed filename and os.replace publish), or explicitly justify the bespoke lock by the crash-degradation / 150s-fallback requirement that filelock's default blocking behaviour does not provide.

findings.checklist_item: Confirm the digest covers every source input render_markdown_to_wiki depends on (or narrow the 'never stale' claim to the pinned inputs), so a renderer change outside wiki_render.py cannot be served a stale artifact.
evidence: Plan: 'The artifact filename embeds a SHA-256 digest of the three corpus JSON files, the wiki_render module source, and the resolved pandoc executable path + size, so a corpus or renderer edit can never be served a stale render.'

wiki_render.py imports/uses helpers (_lock_and_split, _render_unit, _pandoc_path) within the module, but render behavior could also route through other adapter modules not captured by a single-file source hash.
The render is dominated by the pandoc subprocess (pinned via path+size) and this module's own logic, so the practical staleness risk is narrow — but the absolute wording overstates the guarantee.
findings.finding: The staleness guarantee is stated absolutely ('a corpus or renderer edit can never be served a stale render') but the digest only covers the single wiki_render.py module source; render_markdown_to_wiki's output could in principle depend on sibling helper modules it imports, which the digest does not hash.
findings.location: Approach section, digest bullet ('the wiki_render module source')
scenarios: A refactor that moves rendering logic out of wiki_render.py into a sibling module changes output but leaves wiki_render.py source bytes (and thus the digest) unchanged, serving a stale cached artifact.
